title: Regular parameters of the polynomial-append closed source fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $t,e\geq0$, $P_0=k[X_j]$ and $P_1=k[X_j,Y_i]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $p_a\subset P_a$ be prime ideals, let $\iota:P_0\to P_1$ be the first-variable inclusion, assume $p_0=\iota^{-1}(p_1)$ and $Y_i\in p_1$ for every $i$. Let $\alpha:(P_0)_{p_0}\to(P_1)_{p_1}$ be the canonical local map, $J=\mathfrak m_{(P_0)_{p_0}}(P_1)_{p_1}$ and $C=(P_1)_{p_1}/J$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $C$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], has Krull dimension $e$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and its maximal ideal is generated by the ordered list of the $e$ classes of $Y_i/1$.

proof.text: Use the finite-sum variable equivalence followed by the iterated-polynomial equivalence to regard k[X,Y] as P₀[Y]. Transport p₁ to Q along this equivalence. The composite with the first-variable inclusion is the coefficient inclusion, so Q contracts to p₀. The natural localization formula identifies the extended maximal ideals under the localized equivalence; its quotient gives an equivalence of the closed source fibres.

Apply the natural polynomial closed-fibre equivalence to P₀[Y] at Q. It produces a residue-coefficient prime Qk contracting to Q and a natural equivalence with the localization at Qk. Every variable lies in Q by the hypothesis and the reindexing formula, hence every residue-coefficient variable lies in Qk.

The origin ideal is maximal by the polynomial-origin theorem. Since it lies in the proper prime Qk, Qk equals the origin ideal. Compose the fibre equivalences, whose natural formulas send each displayed appended variable to its standard origin variable. The origin theorem gives regular locality, dimension e and generation of the maximal ideal. Transport regular locality and Krull dimension along the ring equivalence. Map the ideal of the displayed list using the variable formula; it is the origin maximal ideal. Mapping ideals by an equivalence is injective, proving generation. This works for e=0 with the empty list and the zero origin ideal.

theorem polynomial_append_closed_fibre_parameters
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (t e : ℕ)
    (p₀ : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin t) k)) [p₀.IsPrime]
    (p₁ : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (t + e)) k)) [p₁.IsPrime]
    (hc : p₀ = p₁.comap (MvPolynomial.rename (Fin.castAdd e)).toRingHom)
    (hz : ∀ i : Fin e, MvPolynomial.X (Fin.natAdd t i) ∈ p₁) :
    let α := Localization.localRingHom p₀ p₁
      (MvPolynomial.rename (Fin.castAdd e)).toRingHom hc
    let J := (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p₀)).map α
    let C := Localization.AtPrime p₁ ⧸ J
    let xs := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin e ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk J
      (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin (t + e)) k) (Localization.AtPrime p₁)
        (MvPolynomial.X (Fin.natAdd t i))))
    ∃ h : IsRegularLocalRing C,
      letI := h
      ringKrullDim C = (e : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
        Ideal.ofList xs = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C
